features.text: The patient fell down outside and experienced chest pain followed by shortness of breath.
The chest pain was described as pressure-like, located in the middle of the chest, and lasted a few minutes.
The chest pain did not radiate and was not associated with sweating, nausea, or dizziness.
The patient experienced shortness of breath after the fall but did not notice any changes in the pattern of shortness of breath since the fall.
The patient tripped and fell, but does not recall hitting his chest or back directly, nor did he experience loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing at the time of the fall.
The patient does not recall any prior cardiac evaluations such as ECGs, stress tests, or echocardiograms.
The patient was told that the echocardiogram showed preserved ejection fraction of 55% and normal diastolic filling, but with mild to moderate mitral regurgitation.
The patient was not previously aware of the mild to moderate mitral regurgitation and does not have a known history of mitral regurgitation or valvular heart disease.
The patient does not recall undergoing any additional imaging studies such as a CT scan of the chest or thoracic spine following the fall.
The patient did not notice any swelling or bruising on his chest or back after the fall.
The patient did not experience palpitations, dizziness, or syncope since the fall.
The patient has a history of hypertension but no prior evaluations for arrhythmias or heart conditions.
The patient did not recall being specifically evaluated for thoracic spine or chest injuries during the ER visit.
The patient did not recall any imaging being performed for thoracic spine or chest injuries during the ER visit.
The patient experienced chest pain and shortness of breath after the fall but did not notice any numbness or tingling in his arms or legs.
